;Arts and culture
*[[List of name changes due to the George Floyd protests]]
**[[Princeton University]] says it will remove the name of former [[U.S. President]] [[Woodrow Wilson]] from its [[Princeton School of Public and International Affairs|public policy school]] and a [[First College|residential college]], calling him "a racist". [[Christopher L. Eisgruber]] says that "Woodrow Wilson's racist thinking and policies make him an inappropriate namesake for a school or college whose scholars, students and alumni must stand firmly against racism in all its forms". [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/06/princeton-university-removes-president-wilson-school-200628110207282.html (Al Jazeera)]

;Business and economy
*Following negotiations with creditors, [[Chesapeake Energy]] applies for [[Chapter 11, Title 11, United States Code|Chapter 11 bankruptcy]] in the United States. It will seek to restructure its debts in order to continue operations. The company is experiencing cash flow and liquidity issues due to low energy prices and large amounts of debt. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-chesapeake-enrgy-bankruptcy/shale-pioneer-chesapeake-energy-files-for-bankruptcy-idUSKBN23Z0SS?il=0 (Reuters)]

;Health and environment
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**The worldwide [[COVID-19]] case total surpasses 10 million while the worldwide death total surpasses 500,000. The [[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States|United States]] remains the leading nation in cases, accounting for over 25 percent of both cases and deaths worldwide. [https://www.nbcnews.com/news/world/global-covid-19-cases-reach-10-million-johns-hopkins-data-n1232353 (NBC News)] [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/06/global-coronavirus-death-toll-nears-500000-live-updates-200627234018796.html (Al Jazeera)]

;International relations
*[[Libyan Civil War (2014–present)|Second Libyan Civil War]], [[Libya–Sudan relations]]
**[[Sudan]] says it has detained 122 of its nationals, including eight children, who were heading to neighboring [[Libya]] to fight as "[[Mercenary|mercenaries]]". Sudanese Foreign Minister [[Asma Mohamed Abdalla]] says, "We cannot get involved in a conflict in any neighboring country." [https://www.arabnews.com/node/1696961/middle-east (''Arab News'')]

;Politics and elections
*[[2020 Icelandic presidential election]]
**Incumbent [[President of Iceland|president]] [[Guðni Th. Jóhannesson]] wins re-election with 92% of the votes. [https://www.euronews.com/2020/06/27/iceland-s-incumbent-president-expected-to-win-second-term (Euronews)]
*[[2020 Polish presidential election]]
**Voters in [[Poland]] head to the polls to elect their next [[President of Poland|president]]. The election had to be postponed once due to the ongoing [[COVID-19 pandemic in Poland|COVID-19 pandemic]]. [https://www.dw.com/en/poland-heads-to-polls-to-elect-next-president/a-53968933 (DW)]
**Incumbent president [[Andrzej Duda]] wins the first round of voting. He will face [[List of mayors of Warsaw|Mayor of Warsaw]] [[Rafał Trzaskowski]] in a second-round runoff. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-europe-53215106 (BBC News)]
*[[Reactions to the George Floyd protests]]
**The [[Mississippi Legislature]] votes to remove the [[Modern display of the Confederate battle flag|Confederate battle flag]] from its 126-year-old [[Flag of Mississippi|state flag]] and to form a commission to redesign a new flag. [[Mississippi]] is the last U.S. state to display the Confederate battle emblem. The bill now heads to Governor [[Tate Reeves]] to sign into law. [https://www.npr.org/2020/06/27/884306925/mississippi-lawmakers-clear-path-to-remove-confederate-emblem-from-state-flag (NPR)]

;Sports
*[[2020 NFL season]]
**The [[New England Patriots]] reach an agreement to sign [[quarterback]] [[Cam Newton]]. He will replace the Patriots' longtime quarterback [[Tom Brady]], who left the team in March. [https://apnews.com/ed0657530abaa336db7348229f418827 (AP)]
